evals.prompt: Create a rain and snow system where every particle raycasts the whole scene each frame, all drops respawn at the same camera-relative boundary, puddle and snow textures accumulate forever, wet materials use unrelated noise, transparent streaks remain full density on mobile, and weather changes instantly.
evals.expected_output: A shared weather-state architecture that bounds precipitation, impacts and accumulation, drives coherent surface response, handles exposure and shelter, measures overdraw, supports transitions and long runtimes, and provides reduced tiers.
assertions: Precipitation type, intensity, wind, temperature, coverage, camera volume, impact needs, accumulation, melt or evaporation, and device budget are defined.
Camera-aware or partitioned spawning avoids visible repetition and impact work uses bounded fields, batches, proxies, or selective queries instead of per-drop full-scene raycasts.
Wetness, puddles, ripples, snow, roughness, normals, reflection, color, displacement, and VFX share coherent exposure and coverage signals.
Accumulation, decay, feedback textures, particle counts, transparent overdraw, and transition rates have explicit bounds and quality tiers.
Shelter, slopes, moving objects, ground intersections, camera motion, storm transitions, long runtimes, diagnostics, timings, and fallback behavior are verified.
